The link is antonyms: austerity is a plain, strict way of life, and luxury is the opposite. Candour (frankness) and deceit are also opposites. Courage and bravery are synonyms, and the rest are unrelated pairs.
The link is a kind and its class: an elegy is a kind of poem, a biography is a kind of book. A chapter is a part of a book, an author makes it, and a library stores it.
The link is a wrong act and what it damages: defamation harms a person's reputation, vandalism harms property. Punishment follows crime, a witness gives testimony, and an archaeologist studies ruins.

The link is a scientist and what he studies: a seismologist studies earthquakes, a meteorologist studies weather. A jockey races on a racecourse, a sculptor uses a chisel and a choreographer directs dancers.
The link is a collector and what he collects: a philatelist collects stamps, a numismatist collects coins. An orator delivers a speech, a jockey rides a horse and a tailor uses a needle.

The link is the opening and the closing of a work: a prologue begins a book and an epilogue ends it, as an overture opens and a finale closes a musical piece. The other pairs link performer and watcher, part and whole, and maker and product.
The link is two opposing sides: the protagonist and antagonist of a story, the plaintiff and defendant in a court case. The other pairs link people who cooperate like an interviewer and an applicant.

The link is a quality and what it deserves: a laudable act deserves praise, a reprehensible act deserves blame. Hazardous is the opposite of safe, and frugal and fertile are not linked to what they deserve.
The link is an eater and its food: a herbivore eats plants, a carnivore eats meat. A camel lives in a desert, a bee in a hive, and a gardener works with soil.
The link is a small piece broken from a whole: a fragment of a whole, a crumb of a loaf. A baker makes bread, a meal ends hunger and a plate sits on a table.

The link is a noun and its adjective: caution gives cautious, courage gives courageous. Brave and bravery are the same words in the reverse order, quick and slow are opposites, and a caterpillar becomes a butterfly.
The link is synonyms: lucid and clear mean the same, as candid and frank do. Hostile and friendly are opposites, and the others link a word to its noun or a maker to a product.

The link is antonyms: a prodigal person spends wastefully, a thrifty one saves. Obstinate and flexible are opposites too. Verbose and wordy are synonyms, and the others link a maker to a product or a leader to his group.
The link is synonyms: clandestine means done in secret. Meticulous and careful have a close meaning. Ancient and modern, and tall and short, are opposites, and a camera is a photographer's tool.
The link is antonyms: a redundant part is not needed, an essential part is needed. Trivial and significant are opposites too. Gloomy and dismal are synonyms, and the others are unrelated links.
The link is a work and its maker: a composer creates a symphony, a sculptor creates a statue. A pen is a writer's tool, a school is a teacher's workplace, and a judge applies law.

The link is 'object and the material it is made of': a chair is made of wood. Window : Glass has the same link, since a window is made of glass. The other pairs show different links: Vast : Huge (word and its synonym); Kilogram : Mass (unit and the quantity it measures); Mechanic : Workshop (worker and workplace).

The link is 'animal and its home': a horse lives in a stable. Dog : Kennel has the same link, since a dog lives in a kennel. The other pairs show different links: Tongue : Taste (organ and its function); Calf : Cow (young animal and its adult); Lenient : Strict (word and its antonym).

The link is 'young animal and its adult': a kitten is the young of a cat. Calf : Cow has the same link, since a calf is the young of a cow. The other pairs show different links: Generous : Stingy (word and its antonym); Hangar : Aeroplane (place and what it stores); Wing : Aeroplane (part and whole).

The link is 'maker and what he makes': a weaver makes cloth. Poet : Poem has the same link, since a poet makes a poem. The other pairs show different links: Heart : Pump (organ and its function); Dove : Peace (symbol and what it stands for); Dog : Kennel (animal and its home).

The link is 'unit and the quantity it measures': the metre is a unit of length. Kilogram : Mass has the same link, since the kilogram is a unit of mass. The other pairs show different links: Baker : Bread (maker and what he makes); Window : Glass (object and the material it is made of); Ear : Hear (organ and its function).

The link is 'unit and the quantity it measures': the litre is a unit of volume. Watt : Power has the same link, since the watt is a unit of power. The other pairs show different links: Doctor : Patient (professional and the person served); Judge : Court (worker and workplace); Fire : Hot (thing and its typical quality).

The link is 'leader and group led': a captain leads a team. Principal : School has the same link, since a principal leads a school. The other pairs show different links: Chef : Kitchen (worker and workplace); Hungry : Starving (weaker and stronger degree of the same feeling or state); Kilogram : Mass (unit and the quantity it measures).

The link is 'unit and the quantity it measures': the kilogram is a unit of mass. Second : Time has the same link, since the second is a unit of time. The other pairs show different links: Tall : Short (word and its antonym); Cow : Moo (animal and its sound); Bird : Nest (animal and its home).

The link is 'cause and effect': practice leads to mastery. Neglect : Decay has the same link, since neglect leads to decay. The other pairs show different links: Composer : Music (maker and what he makes); Shepherd : Flock (leader and group led); Calf : Cow (young animal and its adult).

The link is 'maker and what he makes': a composer makes music. Architect : Building has the same link, since an architect makes a building. The other pairs show different links: Conductor : Orchestra (leader and group led); Optimist : Pessimist (word and its antonym); Rabbit : Burrow (animal and its home).

The link is a counteragent and what it counteracts: an antidote works against poison as a remedy works against an ailment. Hunger and famine are degrees of the same thing, a surgeon uses a scalpel, and a scar results from a wound.

The link is a type of speech or writing and its purpose: a eulogy exists to praise, a satire to ridicule. A hall is the place of a lecture, a stanza is a part of a poem, and an envelope covers a letter.

The link is a person who lacks something: an indigent person lacks wealth, a mute person lacks speech. A fertile field has crops, a miser hoards money and a skilful worker has craft, so none of them lacks it.

The link is a protective measure and the harm it guards against: a vaccine protects against disease, a helmet against injury. A thermometer measures fever, and the other pairs link a worker with a workplace or group.
The link is an office holder and the seat that stands for his authority: a sovereign sits on a throne, a judge on the bench. A rifle and chalk are tools, and a mayor leads a city.
